rules.licence: NSW asks anyone fishing for a Recreational Fishing Fee receipt, and for each fish to be measured against its legal length.
rules.release: Every fish here goes back: the game keeps a log, not a bag.

zones.name: East of the Harbour Bridge
zones.advice: East of the bridge the advice is to eat no more than 150 g of harbour fish a month.

zones.name: West of the Harbour Bridge
zones.advice: West of the bridge nothing caught should be eaten, and catches are to be released. Commercial fishing in the harbour has been closed since 2006.

rigs.name: Prawn under a float
rigs.hint: Close to the wall and the piles, for whatever is feeding there.

rigs.name: Soft plastic on the bottom
rigs.hint: Hopped slowly over the sand for flathead and bream.

rigs.name: Metal lure, cast long
rigs.hint: Out into the current for tailor, trevally and kingfish.

species.name: Yellowtail scad
species.note: Yakkas school round every wharf in the harbour. Most are caught to be bait for something bigger.

species.name: Fan-bellied leatherjacket
species.note: A small mouth and a beak of teeth: it picks a bait off the hook a nibble at a time before it takes it.

species.name: Yellowfin bream
species.note: The harbour's everyday fish, hard against the piles and the oyster-covered rocks, and boldest in low light.

species.name: Luderick
species.note: Blackfish graze the weed on the walls and take a float down slowly. Winter is their season.

species.name: Silver trevally
species.note: Pound for pound the hardest puller on the wharf: it turns side-on and circles all the way in.

species.name: Tailor
species.note: Named for teeth that cut a bait as cleanly as scissors. Schools hunt the harbour at dusk.

species.name: Dusky flathead
species.note: It lies buried in the sand and waits. Over 70 cm it is a breeding female, and the law sends it back.

species.name: Yellowtail kingfish
species.note: The harbour's prize. A hooked king runs for the nearest pile or mooring chain to cut the line on it.

spots.name: Beulah Street Wharf
spots.note: A small public wharf in Kirribilli, straight across from the Opera House. The piles hold yellowtail and trevally, and kingfish come past in summer.
spots.source: Man of Many, Best fishing spots in Sydney (Beulah Street Wharf: squid, yellowtail, trevally)

spots.name: Blues Point Reserve
spots.note: The point at the foot of Blues Point Road, with the bridge to the east and deep water off the rocks. It is west of the bridge, so nothing caught here is for the table.
spots.source: Man of Many, Best fishing spots in Sydney (Blues Point Reserve: trevally, kingfish, jewfish)
